- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of actual trend in high-sentiment periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 0.5–1% per day.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth 3-day moving average before final forecast to reduce noise.
